business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale Remarketing of Secondhand Hydraulic Earthmovers and Rollers

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Hong Kong SAR (foreign investor jurisdiction; the entity is formed as a China-registered Foreign-Invested Partnership under PRC law)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (PRC civil law formation regime for the Foreign-Invested Partnership; Hong Kong SAR common law regime for the investing partner and cross-border documentation)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) and its successive supplementary agreements

Arrangement between the Mainland of China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (Mainland-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of the People's Republic of China on Anti-Money Laundering (2006, as revised, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Ownership Information of Market Entities (State Administration for Market Regulation and People's Bank of China Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019) and its Implementing Regulations; Administrative Measures for the Registration of Foreign-Invested Partnerships (SAMR, 2010); Partnership Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China (2006)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the non-resident corporate general partner or limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registrar of the foreign investor's home jurisdiction (for a Hong Kong investor, the Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Authentication paths are parallel and mutually exclusive. (a) Hague Apostille path for an investor in an Apostille Convention state: notarize the certificate copy before a local notary; obtain an Apostille from the designated Competent Authority; arrange a certified Chinese translation; submit to SAMR and the PRC bank. (b) Consular Legalization path for a non-member state: notarize the certificate; authenticate it through the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs; legalize it through the Chinese Embassy or Consulate; arrange a certified Chinese translation; submit. For a Hong Kong investor using the document in Mainland China, use the Hong Kong China-Appointed Notary Public attestation route with transmission through China Legal Service (Hong Kong) Limited; do not chain apostille and consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Current Standing or Certificate of Incumbency) for the foreign investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home jurisdiction corporate registrar or authorized corporate services provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: (a) Apostille state: notarize the registrar-certified copy; obtain Apostille from the Competent Authority; certified Chinese translation; submit. (b) Non-member state: notarize; authenticate by local Ministry of Foreign Affairs; legalize by Chinese Embassy or Consulate; certified Chinese translation; submit. (c) Hong Kong investor in Mainland China: China-Appointed Notary Public attestation and China Legal Service (Hong Kong) transmission. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be sequentially layered.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution (or equivalent partnership management resolution) authorizing the establishment of the China Foreign-Invested Partnership and execution of the partnership agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors, sole director, or managing partner of the non-resident investing entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: (a) Apostille state: execute the resolution; notarize the directors' or signatories' signatures; obtain Apostille from the Competent Authority; certified Chinese translation; submit. (b) Non-member state: execute; notarize; authenticate by local Ministry of Foreign Affairs; legalize by Chinese Embassy or Consulate; certified Chinese translation; submit. (c) Hong Kong investor: China-Appointed Notary Public attestation and China Legal Service (Hong Kong) transmission. Apostille and consular legalization are exclusive alternatives and must not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Constitutional Charter of the foreign investing entity (certified true copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, registered agent, or legal representative of the foreign investing entity, with registrar countersignature where available
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: (a) Apostille state: certify the copy before a local notary; obtain Apostille from the designated Competent Authority; certified Chinese translation; submit. (b) Non-member state: certify before a notary; authenticate by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs; legalize by Chinese Embassy or Consulate; certified Chinese translation; submit. (c) Hong Kong investor: China-Appointed Notary Public attestation with China Legal Service (Hong Kong) transmission. The apostille and consular legalization paths are parallel, mutually exclusive, and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the non-resident investor (confirming account conduct, financial standing, and source of funds)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank of the foreign investing entity in its home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The original bank letter must be on bank letterhead, signed by the authorized bank officer, and sealed. (a) Apostille state: notarize the officer's signing authority and the bank seal; obtain Apostille; certified Chinese translation; submit. (b) Non-member state: notarize; authenticate by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs; legalize by Chinese Embassy or Consulate; certified Chinese translation; submit. (c) Hong Kong investor: China-Appointed Notary Public attestation and China Legal Service (Hong Kong) transmission. Apostille and consular legalization are not cumulative.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before any formation step, every direct owner, indirect UBO, control person, signatory, and source-of-funds provider in the China Foreign-Invested Partnership must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK Office of Financial Sanctions Implementation list, the PRC MOFCOM Lists of Unreliable Entities and export/import control lists, the PBOC/market supervision UBO risk list, and the Hong Kong designated persons and terrorist financing lists under the United Nations (Anti-Terrorism Measures) Ordinance. Any person identified as a politically exposed person, or a family member or close associate of a PEP, must be subjected to enhanced due diligence, documented source of funds, and senior management approval before admission as a partner. Given the medium-risk trading model involving used construction excavators and payment rails of wire transfer and SWIFT letters of credit, sanctions and PEP screening must be refreshed before each new counterparty transaction, with continuous transaction monitoring for red flags such as round-tripping, suspicious consignee structures, materially over- or under-valued heavy plant, shell company payment routing, or transactions linked to high-risk

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Hong Kong Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance (Cap. 637), sections 5, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 13; Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38), section 7 (partner power to bind the firm) and section 19 (default rules on interests and duties); Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) where a corporate general partner is used.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Registry of Limited Partnership Funds; Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office for business registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LPF1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership Fund) together with the executed Limited Partnership Agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Foreign-Invested Partnership is not subject to any statutory minimum paid-up share capital or capital contribution requirement. Capital commitments are a private contractual matter set out in the Limited Partnership Agreement. No government-blocked escrow account is required for registration. Committed funds must be transferred only upon a valid drawdown notice and must remain traceable through a licensed Hong Kong bank account under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance. A capital commitment schedule must be maintained and made available for the bank’s medium-risk enhanced due diligence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP

1. APPOINTMENT AND QUORUM. At a duly convened meeting of the Board of Directors of the Foreign-Invested Partnership (the "Partnership") held at the registered office in Hong Kong Special Administrative Region on ________, notice having been waived, and with the general partner, authorized representatives and all founding partners present or represented, the Board constituted a quorum and proceeded to consider the formation and governance agenda.

2. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION. RESOLVED, that the Partnership adopts the capital commitments set forth in the executed Limited Partnership Agreement and that the capital subscription schedule, as annexed, be approved, and that the general partner and limited partners are authorized to make capital contributions in accordance with the drawdown requirements of Hong Kong law.

3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the Partnership designate the bank account with ________________, and that the general partner, compliance officer and such other signatories listed in the bank mandate be appointed as authorized signatories, with power to open accounts, maintain deposits, request wire transfers, issue professional payments, execute SWIFT transactions and instruct banks respecting any safe deposits.

4. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Partnership shall be at ________________________________________ in Hong Kong, and that the office complies with the Limited Partnership Fund Ordinance and all service-of-process requirements.

5. STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED, that the officers named for record keeping, anti-money-laundering compliance and beneficial ownership register be appointed, and that the general partner is authorised to file the registration application with the Companies Registry and pay all statutory fees.

6. GENERAL AUTHORITY. RESOLVED, that all officers be and are hereby authorised to execute and deliver certificates, notices, applications, bank instructions and any other instruments necessary to fully implement the foregoing resolutions. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all resolutions are effective as of the date of signing and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance and Reservation for the Foreign-Invested Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry Hong Kong SAR - Integrated Companies Registry e-Services Portal (www.e-cr.com)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search against dormant, existing, and reserved names using the Companies Registry search facility. Propose a unique English and optional Chinese name containing a permitted partnership suffix such as "Limited Partnership Fund" or an abbreviation acceptable to the Registrar. Submit a name reservation application through the Integrated Companies Registry e-Services portal. The requested name must not be prohibited, nor misleadingly similar to an existing registered fund, nor infringe registered trade marks. The Registrar reviews statutory conflict, public interest concerns and potential confusion. Once cleared, the reservation gives the founding partners a temporary priority to proceed with the draft LPA, address consent and bank due diligence while the registration package is finalized.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation form from the Companies Registry portal
Proposed English and optional Chinese name of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
Statement of intended business scope (ISIC 4659 used construction excavators)
Certified copy of the general partner’s identity document or certificate of incorporation
Written authorization from all partners to submit the reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit a written objection to the Companies Registry within 21 days together with a legal opinion on similarity; in the alternative, file a revised name reservation within 3 business days after the written rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Governance Package
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Hong Kong legal counsel and notary public appointed by the partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Limited Partnership Agreement containing capital commitment schedules, profit share, management authority, investment and remarketing scope for used hydraulic earthmovers and rollers, and dispute resolution. Ensure all foreign partners execute under their constitutional capacity; certify passports and corporate resolutions. Prepare a declaration of the lawful source of funds. Attach a beneficial ownership chart and the general partner’s registered office consent. The executed pack becomes the foundational dossier for the Companies Registry filing and for the bank’s AML and KYC review. Legal counsel must attest that the executed documents satisfy Hong Kong statutory requirements and Cap. 637 rules. Any amendment after registration must be notified using the applicable Companies Registry form.
required_dossiers: Fully executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Schedule A capital commitment and distribution waterfall
Certified true copies of all partners’ passports or corporate registration documents
General partner’s consent to act
Registered office address consent form
Beneficial ownership structure chart
Declaration of lawful source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the document package is queried for execution or capacity defects, cure by obtaining legalized signatures and file a supplemental declaration. Re-execute any defective page within 5 business days; the external counsel may issue a certificate of due execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registration of the Limited Partnership Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry Hong Kong SAR - Registry of Limited Partnership Funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form LPF1 together with the executed Limited Partnership Agreement, consent of the general partner, registered office address, and filing fee through the Companies Registry e-Services portal or paper counter. Provide particulars of the general partner and proposed place of business. The Registry checks the availability of the name, processes the statutory fee, and issues the Limited Partnership Registration Certificate upon satisfaction of the statutory prerequisites. After issuance, the Foreign-Invested Partnership acquires its legal identity and can execute contracts, open bank accounts and trade in used construction machinery. The general partner must update any changes to the registered particulars within prescribed deadlines and maintain an annual compliance file.
required_dossiers: Form LPF1
Certificate of name reservation from Step 1
Executed Limited Partnership Agreement
Consent of the general partner to act
Consent to the registered office address
Application filing fee in HKD equivalent to approximately USD 33
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry suspends or queries the application, respond within 14 calendar days with corrected Form LPF1 and supplementary declarations. If rejected, resubmit the corrected application through the Registry’s electronic resubmission channel and pay any resubmission fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Physical Premises Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form IRBR1 and submit the Business Registration application to the Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office within one month of commencing or carrying on business in Hong Kong. Obtain the Business Registration Certificate and, if employees are engaged, complete employer’s return requirements. Submit a tenancy agreement or ownership title for the registered office and any physical warehouse. For allowing storage of used excavators and rollers, undertake a fire safety self-assessment and obtain the Fire Services Department’s confirmation where the premises are subject to a fire service installation certificate. The Business Registration Certificate must be displayed prominently and renewed annually according to the expiration month printed on the certificate.
required_dossiers: Form IRBR1
Limited Partnership Registration Certificate issued in Step 3
Tenancy agreement or ownership title of the registered office and warehouse
General partner’s identity document or passport copy
Fire safety self-assessment where storage of equipment occurs
Business premises photographs and rent receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Office raises an error or penalty, file a revised IRBR1 and pay the correction fee. If the premises are not approved, obtain a new tenancy or lease and submit a cover letter to the Business Registration Office and Fire Services Department within 28 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Filing Governance, AML/CFT and Bank Mandate Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry (TCSP supervision), licensed banks in Hong Kong, and the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit for suspicious transaction reporting
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Foreign-Invested Partnership’s anti-money laundering supervisory arrangements and external trust and company service provider (TCSP) licence with the Companies Registry if a TCSP is used. Appoint a compliance officer and maintain the beneficial ownership register. Open a bank account in the exact legal name of the Partnership and present the Limited Partnership Fund Certificate, Business Registration Certificate, executed Board resolution, AML/CFT policy manual, source of funds declaration and economic substance package. The financial institution will classify the account as medium-risk enhanced due to the use of wire transfers and SWIFT letters of credit in transactions involving used heavy machinery; additional due diligence must cover sanctions, PEP status and trade-based money laundering.
required_dossiers: Executed First Board Resolution
Limited Partnership Registration Certificate
Business Registration Certificate
AML/CFT policy manual and risk assessment
Beneficial ownership register
Bank mandate form and signatory specimen cards
Trade and SWIFT letters of credit documentation templates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines account opening, request an HKMA referral, provide an enhanced due diligence pack, and approach at least two alternative licensed banks. Any TCSP licensing refusal is cured by engaging a licensed TCSP and submitting updated compliance declarations to the Companies Registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Hong Kong Fire Services Department, Environmental Protection Department, Labour Department, and Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office; no sector-specific industrial licensing board exists for ISIC 4659 used heavy machinery remarketing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310); no sector-specific manufacturing or industrial operating permit is required for pure wholesale remarketing of secondhand hydraulic earthmovers and rollers. If open-air storage or warehousing is maintained, a Fire Services Certificate and Dangerous Goods Licence may be mandatory.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD), Hong Kong SAR
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable at the formation stage for a wholesale trading and remarketing licence. No Environmental Impact Assessment is required under the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499) for trading activities. If the operation adds machinery servicing, fuel draining, dismantling or a designated industrial facility, a full EIA report or an EIA permit may become mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater discharge or regulated air emission is authorised from pure trading activity. Any stormwater runoff from storage yards must be controlled; petroleum hydrocarbons in any licensed discharge must not exceed 10 mg/L under the Water Pollution Control Ordinance. VOC emissions from any incidental engine testing must comply with the Air Pollution Control Ordinance using best practicable means. Waste oil, hydraulic fluid and spent batteries must be stored in bunded containment and removed only by licensed waste collectors under the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: People's Republic of China: State Taxation Administration (STA) and its local tax service offices, accessed through the STA electronic taxpayer service platform (e-Tax portal). Hong Kong SAR: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) through the Business Registration Office (BRO) and the eTAX online portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Foreign-Invested Partnership (CN_FIP): (1) Obtain the PRC business license from the Administration for Market Regulation. (2) Within 30 days after license issue, complete tax registration with the competent STA office and obtain or verify the 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is the statutory Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number for the partnership. (3) Register in the STA electronic taxpayer service platform, establish the VAT identity (general taxpayer or small-scale taxpayer), and set invoice quota and invoice issue permissions. (4) For each non-resident foreign partner, register for PRC tax-identification and withholding requirements using the partner's resident-country TIN and tax-residence certificate, because the partnership's income is allocated to partners and taxed at partner level. (5) For Hong Kong, any non-resident person or partnership carrying on business in Hong Kong must apply to the IRD Business Registration Office for a Business Registration Certificate under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) within one month of commencement; the Business Registration Number (BRN) serves as the Hong Kong statutory tax identifier. (6) Since Hong Kong has no VAT/GST, no separate Hong Kong VAT ID is required. If the FIP will act as a PRC exporter, it must additionally obtain the China Customs Registration Code and fulfill any foreign trade enterprise registration requirements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The PRC partnership is transparent for Enterprise Income Tax purposes; profit is taxed at each partner level, not at the partnership entity level. Hong Kong applies territorial profits tax, so offshore trading profits of a Hong Kong-resident partner may remain outside the Hong Kong taxing net if the source of profits is outside Hong Kong.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election for partnerships; pass-through treatment is mandatory. Hong Kong does not provide entity classification elections under the Inland Revenue Ordinance.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Mainland China Value-Added Tax (VAT); Hong Kong has no VAT, GST, or general sales tax, but may apply customs and excise duties on specified goods.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover-based exemption from basic tax registration exists for a licensed PRC partnership. Compulsory VAT general-taxpayer registration is triggered when annual taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000. Small-scale VAT taxpayers with monthly sales up to RMB 100,000 enjoy the VAT exemption threshold while remaining registered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All PRC VAT invoices must be issued through the STA-approved electronic invoice system, including the full digital electronic invoice platform, and uploaded in real time to the national e-invoice database for fiscal clearance. Each invoice must carry the national 20-digit invoice code, encrypted tax-control signature, anti-fraud digital stamp, and one-invoice-one-code unique reference. Hong Kong has no statutory e-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance mandate for VAT purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Mainland China leg: the exported used construction excavators must be physically shipped from the PRC customs territory to an overseas destination; the CN_FIP must be the exporter named in the customs export declaration, hold valid PRC customs and foreign trade registration, maintain a genuine commercial sale to an offshore buyer settled by wire transfer or letter of credit, and present completed export customs clearance evidence. The sale is then eligible for 0% VAT with refund of creditable input VAT, or exemption-only treatment for used fixed assets where no input VAT was deductible. Hong Kong leg: no VAT is levied in Hong Kong, so no zero-rating claim is required; the relevant Hong Kong issue is territorial profits tax treatment of offshore trading income.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Export sales contract and commercial invoice issued by the CN_FIP
Packing list with hydraulic excavator and roller serial numbers, model, condition, and HS code evidence
PRC Customs export release and clearance record or manifest printout
Foreign exchange collection record, bank receipt, or SAFE trade-monitoring verification record
Used machinery inspection and condition report supporting the declared used-goods status
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export cannot be substantiated with customs, transport, inventory, or foreign exchange evidence, or if the proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day statutory deadline, the STA will reverse the 0% VAT rate, assess output VAT at the standard goods rate of 13% on the export invoice, claw back any input VAT refunded, charge late-payment interest, and impose penalties under the PRC Tax Collection Administration Law of up to five times the tax evaded or fraudulently refunded in export-rebate fraud cases. False customs declarations may also trigger customs penalties, suspension or loss of export VAT refund qualifications, corporate credit blacklisting, and criminal referral for export tax fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and its delegated State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) for the mainland Foreign-Invested Partnership; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) as the offshore monetary authority for Hong Kong-dollar clearing corridors.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The mainland FIP operates under the PRC foreign exchange control framework, where the RMB is convertible for current-account transactions such as trade in used construction machinery and associated logistics, but capital-account transactions remain controlled and require SAFE registration, bank-level authenticity verification, and tax clearance before remittance. Inbound capital contributions from foreign partners are treated as direct investment and must be injected through a SAFE-registered FDI capital account, with the funds ultimately subject to the FIP's approved business scope. Outbound profit or income distributions are generally viewed as current-account investment income and can be remitted after the corporate income tax filing, audited financial statements, and proof of source and legitimacy are presented, whereas the return of partnership capital or liquidation proceeds requires a capital-account deregistration and a separate SAFE remittance filing. Hong Kong itself has no exchange controls, but because the treasury must bring funds into and out of mainland China, the binding constraint is PBOC/SAFE convertibility. Export proceeds derived from wholesale remarketing of used earthmovers must be repatriated to the mainland FIP's foreign-exchange settlement account; the entity may elect to keep up to 100% of those proceeds in foreign currency and settle into RMB on demand, subject to trade authenticity verification through invoices, customs declarations, and bills of lading. The resulting treasury design should therefore operate a two-layer liquidity matrix: an onshore SAFE-compliant RMB and foreign-exchange settlement layer at a designated Chinese bank, and an offshore HKD/USD treasury and documentary trade layer in Hong Kong governed by HKMA rules but not by PRC convertibility restrictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the current SAFE zero-surrendrance framework, the FIP must repatriate export proceeds into its mainland foreign-exchange settlement account within 180 days from the customs declaration or the agreed contractual trade settlement date, whichever is later, as supported by the underlying sales contract and customs records. There is no mandatory conversion ratio: 0% of export receipts must be converted, and 100% may be retained in foreign currency. Conversion to RMB may be executed on demand through the designated bank's settlement-and-sale system, provided the bank can verify the export invoice, customs declaration, bill of lading, and proof of payment from the overseas buyer.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI) + RMB Basic Deposit Account + Foreign Exchange Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account + Multi-Currency Operating Account + Export Proceeds Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account for Partnership Contribution + Trade Settlement Account supporting SWIFT MT103 and MT700 flows

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to nil as a primary account. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Airwallex, Revolut Business, Currenxie, and Aspire are not licensed by PBOC/SAFE to open the mandatory SAFE-monitored foreign-exchange settlement account, process FDI capital registrations, execute RMB settlement-and-sale, or serve as the FIP's primary tax-filing banking relationship. They may be used only as ancillary collection and disbursement channels in Hong Kong for non-mainland transactions, and all funds that enter or leave mainland China must be routed through a licensed mainland commercial bank. Using an offshore EMI as the main treasury account would create a serious SAFE audit defect and a withholding tax and transfer-pricing hazard for the FIP.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a mainland foreign-invested partnership, at least one authorised representative of the managing general partner must physically attend the opening branch for the initial KYC, OFAC/sanctions screening, and underwriting interview. Remote consular proxy opening is not a generally accepted PBOC/SAFE standard for the primary RMB basic deposit account, FDI capital escrow account, or foreign-exchange settlement account. Where the general partner is a Hong Kong company, the bank may accept a certified board resolution, Companies Registry business registration, certificate of incumbency, and notarised partnership agreement in advance, but the interviewed individual must be a named signatory presenting original passport or HK identity documents and the original seal chops to be lodged at the branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chain with a Hong Kong corporate general partner sitting above a pass-through partnership, creating shell or wealth-routing risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full beneficial-owner chart tracing to natural persons, HK Companies Registry business registration and annual return, certificate of incumbency, notarised partnership agreement, source-of-wealth statements for each beneficial owner including 24 months of bank statements and audited financials, signed source-of-funds declaration, and a written commercial purpose narrative that ties the HK structure to used heavy-machinery trading.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering red flag in used construction machinery, including over/under-invoicing, serial-number mismatches, or commingled new and used equipment shipments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original vendor and end-customer contracts, commercial invoices with precise HS codes and unit prices, customs export/import declarations, bills of lading or airway bills, manufacturer or auction title certificates for each excavator unit, independent third-party equipment appraisal and inspection reports, and a serial-number reconciliation ledger linking each purchase contract to the underlying physical asset.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through partnership may be viewed as a vehicle for distributing profits to foreign partners while avoiding mainland enterprise income tax and withholding obligations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI registration confirmation, annual audited PRC GAAP financial statements, partnership income tax returns with payment receipts, tax clearance certificates from the competent mainland tax authority, partner capital account records, board or partner resolutions for each distribution, and the FIP business license clearly reflecting wholesale trading of secondhand machinery and equipment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Secondary-market auction and cash-like settlement patterns may indicate round-tripping, invoice fraud, or third-party collection risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Auction-platform account statements and buyer verification reports, bank statements showing the original overseas funds entering the FIP, signed sales and purchase contracts with delivery milestones, inspection certificates from licensed heavy-machinery testing agencies, an independent anti-money-laundering review of the transaction monitoring system, and a list of known counterparties with sanctions-screening results.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign partners must remit capital from their HKD or USD bank accounts in Hong Kong to the FIP's SAFE-registered foreign-exchange capital account at the designated mainland bank using SWIFT MT103 with the SAFE-approved direct-investment purpose code and the FDI registration certificate number referenced in the remittance narrative. The receiving bank will perform the capital-account confirmation through the SAFE information system, credit the funds, and upon request convert the foreign currency into RMB through the bank's settlement-and-sale platform. The RMB capital settlement balance can then be used strictly for operational expenses within the FIP's approved business scope, such as used excavator purchases, spare parts, freight, insurance, salaries, rent, and trade finance charges. A certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report after the funds are credited to evidence the paid-in partnership capital and support subsequent bank credit facilities or documentary trade applications.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements, the FIP should use a layered clearing model. Import disbursements for secondhand construction equipment can be made through SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for advance-payment or open-account terms, through irrevocable commercial letters of credit issued via SWIFT MT700 under UCP600 for large or multi-unit purchases, or through documentary collections under URC522 using SWIFT MT400 for seller-drawn drafts against documents. Export collections from overseas buyers will enter the mainland FIP's foreign-exchange settlement account via SWIFT MT103 or via an LC advising/confirming bank and subsequent presentation. The clearing bank must obtain the underlying trade documents before settling, including the commercial invoice, bill of lading, inspection certificate, customs declaration, and the FIP business registration, so that the transaction can be recorded in SAFE's current-account trade monitoring system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB deliverable FX forward contracts (CNY/USD and CNY/HKD) with the account bank under SAFE current-account trade-receivables and trade-payables hedging rules, strictly capped at underlying trade and working-capital exposure.

Foreign exchange swaps (CNY/USD or CNY/HKD) for temporary liquidity alignment between the onshore RMB settlement layer and the offshore HKD/USD treasury balances, supported by a documented working-capital or trade-payment cycle.

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CNY/USD or CNY/HKD) for medium-term HK-funded trade-finance or capital-expenditure hedging, provided the notional matches the FIP/HK funding corridor and no speculative or leveraged overlay is created.

Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) may be executed by the Hong Kong financing vehicle to hedge RMB exposure, subject to HKMA margin and KYC rules, but the mainland FIP itself may not use onshore NDFs because RMB is deliverable and speculative NDF structures are not permitted under SAFE.

Bang-bang or participative structured forwards are permissible only where the structure does not embed a barrier that creates a leverage or option-like payoff beyond the real trade exposure, and only after written approval from the relationship bank's derivatives compliance desk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Hong Kong Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date printed on the current Business Registration Certificate; renewal cycle is every 12 months from the certificate issue date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal attracts an additional fee of HKD 300; carrying on business without a valid certificate is prosecutable with fines up to HKD 5,000 and daily default fines; continued non-compliance leads to removal from the Business Register and administrative enforcement against each partner.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return for Partnership or Corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Return is issued on 1 April or on a rolling basis by the Inland Revenue Department; filing is due within one month of the issue date, subject to any electronic filing extension granted by the Commissioner.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file can result in estimated assessments, late filing penalties under the Inland Revenue Ordinance, fines up to HKD 10,000 and additional penalties up to three times the tax undercharged where the default is attributable to fraud or wilful neglect.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employers' Return of Remuneration and Pensions (BIR56A and BIR56B)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 30 April, being within one month after the end of the 31 March tax year; a nil return is required where applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the employer to fines up to HKD 10,000; continued default may lead to estimated assessments and prosecution, with additional penalties for incorrect or incomplete returns.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (NAR1) if the vehicle is converted to or formed as a private company; not required for a pure partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of incorporation for a private company; the return must state company particulars as at the anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers fixed late fees ranging from HKD 870 to HKD 3,480 depending on the period of delay; prosecution may follow, and the Registrar may strike off a defunct or non-filing company after due process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership Annual Report and Foreign Investment Information Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, with information shared with commerce authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually from 1 January to 30 June covering the preceding calendar year; no statutory extension is available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file results in inclusion on the abnormal operations list; non-rectification for three consecutive years leads to inclusion on the serious untrustworthy list and possible administrative revocation of the partnership registration; misrepresentation attracts administrative fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual PRC Tax Filing, Partnership Income Allocation Statements and Supporting Accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Chinese State Taxation Administration / local competent tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual enterprise tax filings are generally due by 31 May for the preceding calendar year; partnership income allocation schedules and individual partner annual comprehensive income reconciliations are due by 30 June where applicable.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of up to CNY 2,000 per return and late payment surcharges of 0.05% per day apply; understatement penalties range from 0.5 to 5 times the tax evaded, and deliberate non-filing can trigger tax authority enforcement and partner-level criminal liability.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For Hong Kong corporate-form entities, statutory audit is mandatory unless the entity is a small private company satisfying at least two of the following three conditions for the current and immediately preceding financial year: annual turnover not exceeding HKD 10,000,000; total assets not exceeding HKD 10,000,000; and headcount not exceeding 50 employees. If the entity is a public company, a group member required to prepare consolidated accounts, or a company whose articles require audit, no exemption applies and a licensed certified public accountant must perform the audit under Part 9 of the Companies Ordinance. For the PRC foreign-invested partnership, the annual foreign investment information report and local tax authorities may require a Chinese CPA-audited annual financial report where the partnership's operations exceed the local turnover, asset or employee tolerances for simplified filing; bank financing and partner-level tax audits also trigger a statutory audit certificate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) aligned with IFRS; HKFRS for Private Entities is available to eligible small private entities; PRC onshore operations and statutory annual reporting follow Chinese Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (ASBE) with reconciliations to HKFRS where group or Hong Kong reporting requires consistency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not require an annual UBO declaration to the Companies Registry; however, the Significant Controllers Register must be maintained at the registered office and updated within 7 days of any notifiable change. For the PRC foreign-invested partnership, the annual report filed by 30 June serves as the annual confirmation of partner and beneficial ownership particulars, and any transfer of partnership interests or change in capital structure must be registered with the relevant market regulation authority within the statutory 30-day reporting window.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors / General and Limited Partners

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,500 per year for a Hong Kong registered office and licensed corporate secretarial agent; USD 400 - USD 1,200 per year for a PRC registered address and local filing agent.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 10,000 for the Hong Kong holding or partnership wrapper; USD 6,000 - USD 18,000 if a combined PRC foreign-invested partnership audit and annual reporting package is required.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Foreign-Invested Partnership is fiscally transparent under Caishui 2008 No. 159 and pays no corporate income tax at entity level; corporate partners pay CIT at 25%. A corporate partner that qualifies as a small low-profit enterprise can enjoy an effective 5% rate on the first RMB 3 million of annual taxable income, while High and New Technology Enterprises may use a 15% reduced rate. No free-zone patent box or used-machinery trading tax holiday is applicable. A 100% R&D super deduction applies only to qualified corporate partner R&D expenses and not to trading inventory.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Corporate Income Tax Annual Return Form A100000 and quarterly prepayment Form A200000, filed through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax filing portal (e-Tax). The FIP prepares an annual income allocation schedule for its partners; each corporate partner includes its distributive share on its own Form A100000.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly CIT prepayments must be paid within 15 days after the close of each quarter; the annual corporate income tax reconciliation and final tax payment are due on or before May 31 following the calendar year-end, or within five months after an approved non-calendar fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue from the wholesale remarketing of used construction excavators and rollers, including domestic sales and export sales of secondhand hydraulic earthmovers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognize revenue under PRC enterprise income tax realization rules and the invoice value stated under PRC VAT rules; exclude output VAT and customs duties collected on the goods. A non-resident corporate partner should report its distributive share only after the FIP allocation schedule is completed. Cross-border sales invoiced through a Hong Kong booking affiliate will be challenged unless the revenue allocation corresponds to actual functions, assets and risks.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, including acquisition cost of used excavators, freight, inspection, reconditioning labor and direct logistics expenses attributable to the traded machinery.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only actual costs supported by purchase invoices and customs declarations. If excavators are imported from a Hong Kong related seller, the purchase price must be arm-length under PRC transfer pricing rules; an excessive intercompany cost will be adjusted and may attract a penalty from 50% to 5 times of the underpaid tax under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible selling, general and administrative expenses, including commissions, freight, warranty, office rent, professional fees and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only expenses that are ordinary, reasonable and supported by compliant invoices or receipts. Management fees charged by the Hong Kong parent to the PRC FIP are deductible only if they satisfy the arm-length benefit test and are not pure profit distributions. Payments for royalties or interest to Hong Kong must be reflected on the withholding schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating profit before tax adjustments, computed as Box 1 minus Box 2 minus Box 3.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident partner, do not simply use the FIP accounting profit. Apply the special tax adjustment rules for related-party transactions and assess whether the FIP is a permanent establishment of the Hong Kong partner. If a PE exists, the partner files a CIT return at 25% and may not rely on a treaty business-profit exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjustments for tax-exempt income, non-deductible expenses, losses and carryover items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back entertainment expenses, fines, penalties, undistributed profits and other prohibited deductions. The FIP itself cannot claim corporate tax incentives; only the partner can apply preferential rates. A foreign partner with no PE may instead be subject to gross-basis withholding rather than filing a reconciled CIT return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments and loss offset for the corporate partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the five-year tax loss carryforward at partner level. Losses allocated from the FIP are usable only by the partner receiving the allocation and may not be transferred to other group entities. A non-resident partner should not use the loss to shelter China-source income not allocable to its PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT payable at the statutory rate or reduced treaty rate, less prepayments and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Corporate partners pay 25% on allocated taxable income if the FIP activity is attributable to a mainland China PE. If no PE exists and the income is China-source, the payer must withhold and remit 10% under the PRC CIT Law. A Hong Kong partner may claim a reduced rate only by filing DTA relief documents before withholding, including a Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership proof.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership allocation schedule and cross-border related-party transactions disclosure.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the FIP profit distribution agreement, intercompany contracts, transfer pricing benchmarking evidence and withholding tax vouchers for interest, royalties or profit remittances. This schedule is the first place a China tax inspector will test whether the non-resident partner truly has Hong Kong economic substance or is merely a treaty-shopping conduit.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or inaccurate CIT return risks include: a RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000 late-filing fine, up to RMB 50,000 for serious non-compliance; an overdue daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax from the due date to payment; and for tax evasion under Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law, a penalty from 50% to 5 times the tax underpaid plus recovery of tax. Criminal liability can arise under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law where undeclared or falsely declared tax is large, generally exceeding RMB 100,000 and more than 10% of the tax payable; aggravated tax evasion can lead to imprisonment of three to seven years. Responsible persons may also be placed on the cross-departmental joint blacklist and banned from leaving the PRC.
